title: Policy for dealing in securities

tiers.name: Directors and officers
tiers.description: All directors and officers of the Group, including the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). For approval purposes this group splits into the Chair of the Board and other directors (including the CEO).

tiers.name: Senior executives
tiers.description: All direct reports to the CEO.

tiers.name: Other employees
tiers.description: Other employees of the Group as determined by the Board from time to time.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Employee (spouse, partner, children, children of the partner, or dependants) and a company or other entity the Employee has an ability to control. The Employee (not the Connected Person) must do any act required by the Policy, e.g. obtaining clearance, on the Connected Person's behalf.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished from other directors and officers only for the approval chain (informs and obtains approval from the Board or the Chair of the ARCC) and as an approver of exceptional-circumstances waivers for other directors/officers and senior executives.

definitions.hedging_definition: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 30 June each year (or the last trading day before that day)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement to ASX of the preliminary final statement or full year results

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 31 December each year (or the last trading day before that day)
windows.end_anchor: the day following the announcement of the half-yearly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify any other blackout period from time to time (clause 3.2(a)); the Policy does not state whether such additional periods are kept confidential.

rules.detail: Securities is defined to extend to financial products issued or created over or in respect of Company securities, whether created by the Company or third parties, with no venue limitation, so an OTC put/call is caught. Derivatives (exchange-traded options, CFDs, other derivatives) are expressly named as prohibited during blackout periods; outside blackout periods they are a 'dealing' requiring approval under 3.3.
rules.evidence: For the avoidance of doubt, during the above periods Relevant Persons must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (for example, exchange-traded options, contracts for differences and other derivatives).

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging unvested equity held under any employee, executive or director equity plan; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged prior to the vesting of those Company securities. In particular, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into any hedge transaction involving unvested equity held pursuant to any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging vested Company securities that remain subject to a plan holding lock or dealing restriction; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of any employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested and unrestricted Company securities is expressly permitted, treated as a dealing requiring the same approval and notification under 3.3, and not to be entered into while in possession of inside information.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are permitted to hedge their vested and unrestricted Company securities on the following conditions: (1) the hedge transaction is treated as a dealing in Company securities for the purposes of this Policy, and the relevant approvals and notifications are made on this basis.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (e.g. prepaid forward sale) are not named. 'Securities' extends to financial products created over Company securities and 'dealing' includes agreements to buy or sell, so a monetisation transaction is a dealing requiring approval under 3.3 and is barred in blackout periods and while holding inside information.
rules.evidence: the term 'securities' also extends to financial products issued or created over or in respect of securities issued by the Company (for example, warrants and other derivative products), whether or not the financial products are created by the Company or by third parties.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Policy or Attachment 1, and is not listed as an example of prohibited or short-term dealing.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

Contracts for differences are expressly named as an example of financial products caught by the blackout prohibition; outside blackout periods a CFD is a dealing requiring approval and would also be caught by the short-term/speculative dealing restriction if opened and closed within 3 months.
rules.evidence: during the above periods Relevant Persons must not deal in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities (for example, exchange-traded options, contracts for differences and other derivatives).

rules.detail: Blanket ban on dealing in Company securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement, with no security-state or approval carve-out.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not deal in the Company's securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Granting a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities is not named outside the specific margin lending prohibition in 3.4, and the dealing definition does not expressly mention encumbrance.

The Policy only names 'margin lending arrangements' as prohibited; it does not use a broader term such as 'secured financing arrangement'. Whether a bespoke loan secured on Company securities that is not itself a 'margin lending arrangement' is caught is not expressly stated, but exclusion 3.6(e) (a forced sale by 'a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement' is only excused 'subject to paragraph 3.4') indicates the Policy treats secured lending over Company securities generally as within the intent of the 3.4 ban.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not deal in the Company's securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: Ban on buying and selling on market within a 3 month period and on entering other short-term dealings such as forward contracts; participation in an employee/executive/director equity plan is excluded from this and other restrictions in 3.2/3.3.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

clearance.approver: the Board or the Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee (ARCC)
clearance.post_trade_to: the Board or the Chair of the ARCC (as applicable) and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: the Chair of the Board must inform and obtain approval from the Board or the Chair of the ARCC before a transaction is undertaken.

clearance.post_trade_to: the Chair of the Board and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: any other director of the Company (including the CEO) must inform and receive approval from the Chair of the Board before a transaction is undertaken.

clearance.post_trade_to: the CEO and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: any other Relevant Person must inform and receive approval from the CEO before a transaction is undertaken.

clearance.post_trade_to: the CEO and the Company Secretary
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the dealing
clearance.evidence: any other Relevant Person must inform and receive approval from the CEO before a transaction is undertaken.

short_term.basis: buying and selling on market within the period
carve_outs: participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company (clause 3.6(a))
short_term.evidence: Relevant Persons must not deal in the Company's securities on a short-term trading basis. Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short-term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board, Chair of the ARCC, or the CEO (as relevant), or their delegate
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances for these purposes includes severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the approver.

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board, Chair of the ARCC, or the CEO (as relevant), or their delegate
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances for these purposes includes severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order or any other circumstance that is deemed exceptional by the approver.
participation in an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by the Company (eg applying for an allocation of securities under an employee equity plan offer).

acquisition of Company securities through a dividend reinvestment plan; acquisition of Company securities through a share purchase plan available to all retail shareholders; and acquisition of Company securities through a rights issue
the disposal of Company securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

dealings that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the securities (for example, transfers of Company securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Relevant Person is a beneficiary)

trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan, where the Relevant Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a blackout period, the plan does not permit the Relevant Person to exercise any influence or discretion in relation to trading under the plan and the plan cannot be cancelled during a blackout period, other than in exceptional circumstances
subject to paragraph 3.4, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a Relevant Person dealing in units or shares of a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange-traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party and that happens to hold as part of its portfolio securities in the Company.

exemption_authority: The Chair of the Board, the Chair of the ARCC, or the CEO (as relevant), or their delegate, may grant a written waiver from the blackout period restrictions for exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, compulsion by court order, or another circumstance deemed exceptional), valid for 2 business days and otherwise subject to the rest of the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons may not deal in the Company's securities pursuant to a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is banned if characterised as a 'margin lending arrangement'; the term is undefined, so whether a bespoke bilateral loan secured on the collared shares escapes the ban is untested and should be cleared with the Chair/CEO before proceeding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to paragraph 3.4, a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This exclusion removes a lender's enforcement sale from the blackout and approval requirements in 3.2 and 3.3, but only 'subject to paragraph 3.4', so it does not rescue a financing arrangement that is itself a prohibited margin loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Hedging includes entering into transactions in financial products that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A purchased put and written call collar squarely fits this definition; it is permitted with clearance only over vested and unrestricted shares, and never over unvested or holding-locked vested shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a waiver is granted... the duration of the waiver to deal in securities will be 2 business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar entered under an exceptional-circumstances waiver during a blackout period must be fully executed within 2 business days, a tight window for documenting a bank collar and loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances, could my proposed transaction be perceived by the market as me (or my Connected Persons) taking advantage of my position in an inappropriate way?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a formally compliant collar must be self-assessed for negative market perception, and any concerns must be flagged in the approval request, giving the approver discretion to refuse or condition clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where a Relevant Person enters into a hedging arrangement in respect of Company securities, the Company may, where appropriate, disclose the fact and nature of the hedge (eg in its annual report or to ASX).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank and executive should expect the collar's existence and terms could be publicly disclosed by the Company in its annual report or to ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a company or any other entity which the Employee has an ability to control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the loan or collar through a controlled entity or trust does not avoid the Policy's approval requirements or the margin lending ban, since Connected Persons' dealings are treated as the Employee's own.

summary: A funded collar is workable only over vested and unrestricted Regis shares: unvested shares and vested shares still under a plan holding lock can never be hedged, and even permitted hedges of vested unrestricted shares are treated as a 'dealing' requiring prior approval (Board/ARCC Chair for the Chair; Chair of the Board for other directors; CEO for senior executives and other employees), execution within 2 business days of approval, and avoidance of blackout periods (30 June and 31 December to results release) and any period the person holds inside information. The loan leg is the key obstacle: clause 3.4 bans 'margin lending arrangements' using Company securities as security, and while a bespoke bank loan secured on the collared shares may not be a literal margin loan, the Policy's forced-sale exclusion (available only 'subject to paragraph 3.4') suggests secured lending over Company securities generally is not intended to be permitted, so structuring and approval risk falls on the loan. No minimum shareholding requirement or standing financing-disclosure obligation is stated, but the Company may separately disclose the hedge's existence in its annual report or to ASX, and each dealing must be confirmed to the Company Secretary within 2 business days. Tenor should exceed three months given the short-term dealing prohibition. Overall verdict: the derivative legs are achievable with clearance on vested, unrestricted shares in an open window, but the secured-loan leg needs an explicit, favourable ruling from the Chair of the Board or CEO that it is not a prohibited 'margin lending arrangement'.
